name: Anime
visualIdentity: Explicitly described as a coherent anime character-design and rendering language: stable proportions, expressive poses, clean linework, controlled shadow shapes, and selectively detailed action. Anime is not one uniform aesthetic; a cel-shading filter alone is not character animation.
suitableUses: Suitable for illustrated mascots, expressive character scenes, and product or explainer stories with existing character art. Inferred: key poses and held expressions can suit introductions or narrative beats. For interactive HTML, bounded facial responses or scroll-led scenes can work when artwork supports them.
limitations: Requires consistent character drawings or prepared frames; report missing character assets rather than substituting a filter. Avoid mixed anime design languages, warped proportions, eye distortion, or motion that distracts. Omit gaze-following if readable eyes, layers, or a rig are absent. Do not use parallax alone to imply character animation.
palette: No canonical palette is specified. Resolve colors from task instructions, brand or approved references, existing semantic mappings, then the optional example: background #F4EFE5, foreground #293447, accents #668DA0 and #C47C67. Preserve exact supplied colors, character-model palette, color families, and role assignments; keep tokens discrete, with no proposed gradient. Accent text pairings fail the stated 4.5 normal-text contrast target, so use accents decoratively and verify actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Plan key poses, expressive holds, and selectively detailed action. For video, derive all states from seekable composition time; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, and reading holds. Optional interactive patterns include bounded pointer-led pupils with neutral recovery, or scroll-linked chapter/story states that reverse coherently. These require suitable assets; live input is for HTML, not video.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices. Keep speech intelligible, avoid competing vocals and clipping, synchronize audio and picture, and inspect them together.
assetRequirements: Prepare consistent character drawings or numbered transparent PNG frames, preserving alpha, dimensions, and clear naming; Krita is a suggested drawing and frame-sequence tool. Optional motion may require eye layers or a rig. No specific audio assets are supplied.
combinations: Can pair with style-101 painted background planes for layered movement under held character poses, keeping character palette, lighting direction, and proportions consistent. Can pair with style-112 diegetic HUD only in sci-fi scenes, inside device frames and away from faces; use #293447, #668DA0, #C47C67 without added neon. These are conditional suggestions, not defaults.
productionApproach: Select visual and motion methods for the art and action first; drawing/frame preparation owns the character visuals, and a suitable motion layer owns movement. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; Remotion is only a documented fallback when unavailable or unable to meet a required capability. Keep video deterministic and seekable; for interactive HTML, map scroll or pointer input to coherent states. Verify representative frames, full playback, dimensions, frame rate, loop continuity, and audio sync.
